В системе GENESIS это магический «женски: In GENESIS this is a magical ‘feminine’ year: its inner fabric is defined not by the months and weeks of the solar year, but by the Moon's growth, fullness, and outflow. Это современная символическая система GE: This is a modern symbolic GENESIS system, not a reconstruction of one universal ancient Greek calendar. Its ancient grounding is Selene as a heavenly sign for mortals and the Moon's mid-month fullness in the Homeric Hymn; Greek lunisolar calendars did keep lunar months aligned with the seasons by intercalating a month.

Лунный месяц начинается новолунием. Осно: A lunar month begins at the new moon. Lunar days form its primary rhythm, while Gregorian and sacred dates remain visible. The lunar year begins with the first new moon after the spring equinox.
Современный григорианский календарь — пр: The modern Gregorian calendar is a profane civil system with a layered history. Its months and reckoning of the year were inherited from Rome. The roots of the seven-day week reach back to ancient Babylon: Babylonian astrology gave special significance to the seven visible celestial bodies. The seven-day rhythm reached Rome through two traditions: the Jewish Sabbath week and the Greco-Roman planetary week. In the ancient world, weekdays acquired celestial patrons—the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn—and the sacred character of each day began to take shape. The tradition of celebrating New Year on January 1 also came from Rome and was not invented by one person. January was associated with Janus, the god of doorways, transitions, and beginnings. In 153 BCE, the consuls' accession to office was moved to that date so they could depart earlier for the war in Hispania; because years were named after consuls, January 1 became the beginning of the civil year, and Julius Caesar's reform established the tradition. In 1582, Pope Gregory XIII introduced the reform named after him to correct the accumulated drift of the Julian calendar and restore the vernal equinox for the ecclesiastical calculation of Easter. The modern calendar therefore unites Babylonian-Jewish, Greco-Roman, Roman civil, and Christian ecclesiastical heritage. In the symbolic system of GENESIS, Cronus serves as the patron of this chronology—the image of time, measure, limits, and the inexorable course of cycles. Saturday is understood here as a sacred day of obligatory rest: a time to cease ordinary work, restore the body, and return to inner stillness. This practice resonates with the Jewish Shabbat—the seventh day on which work is set aside and the day is devoted to God.
